lines.en: “Why?” you ask? I do not know. But she seems to have a destination in mind and I seem to be both spineless and aimless, so I follow her without question.
Through the tunnels, down the tracks, and eventually onto the streets of the urban district that, while normally crowded for Kumon-mi, seem somewhat desolate tonight.
If she were a normal girl, I’m sure I’d be able to hear her walking beside me right now. But it’s only my footsteps that make any noise, and that tells me one of two things.
Either her forcefully trained elegance is impressive enough to conceal her presence and indefinitely hide her in plain sight-
Or she’s just good enough at matching my pace to develop new levels of both synchronicity and synchronization that seem otherwise tragically spurious.
It makes me glad Carl Jung isn’t here. For he might try to take her from me. And she might follow for he’d be better for her.
Apart from the whole “death” thing, that is. But based on her affinity for horror, I feel like that might be less of an issue than I initially believed.
: Just out of curiosity, what are your thoughts on necrophilia?
: Just out of curiosity, why are you curious?
: Are you in favor or not? Just answer the question.
: Not.
: Not even for that one guy you like?
: No, the other one.
: American movie star, Seth Rogen? Did I even tell you about that?
: Yeah. If that guy was dead-
: Sensei, I’m not sure what you’re getting at, but I don’t think you’re going to be able to talk me into supporting sexual intercourse with a corpse.
: I don’t know, Touka. I did manage to talk you into thinking you needed to perform a special chant to operate a vending machine before.
: That may be true. But I am much smarter now than I was back then, and I’m hard-pressed to believe you could talk me into anything at all anymore.
: I also talked you into thinking condoms need to be refrigerated just a couple of hours ago.
: You mean to tell me this was a lie and I ate a refrigerated condom for nothing?
: ...Did you actually eat one?
: You told me I could and I was hungry.
: You are far more broken than I thought you were.
: And you are just as easy to convince as me. Of course I did not eat a condom. And of course I would not have sex with the corpse of anyone.
: I mean, why would I agree to such a thing when I don’t even know what sexual intercourse with the living feels like yet? You know, on account of the man I admire seeing me as a mother and all.
: This changes nothing. It just makes the sex conceptually weirder.
: Probably not as weird as you think. I looked deeper into it and found that Oedipal complexes aren’t all that uncommon in men after all. In fact, I may even be willing to embrace this role now.
: Assuming you allow me to, of course. Even now, you seem quite hesitant when it comes to touching me.
: Did I scare you by holding your hand earlier? Was that too forward?
: I was mostly just surprised you did it right in front of Yasu.
: Yasu is, as peculiar as it is to say, my best friend. I don’t mind if she knows about my feelings for you.
: And frankly, I don’t really care if anyone knows at this point. I entered the game very late and if this is what I must do to win, so be it.
: Besides, if I don’t, I’m beginning to think my mother will. Her obsession with you is becoming quite ridiculous, I must say.
: Oh, good. So it’s not just me who thinks that.
: Yeah, your mom is weird. And confusing. And scary. Like you, just turned up to eleven instead of like...two.
: Two? I’m far scarier than that. Do not underestimate my power just because I want to sleep with you.
: Technically speaking, I could have you kidnapped and forced into sexual slavery without anyone even knowing it happened. You should keep that in mind.
: It’s hard not to when it feels sometimes like that’s what your mom has planned on doing with me from the start.
: Hah...while it’s true that there may be some physical attraction at play here, I don’t think it’s the root cause of her obsession.
: Well, what is then? Because your insight is obviously far better than mine on account of actually knowing how she operates.
: It seems almost debt-motivated to me. Similar to the ways in which she’s apparently attached to Yumi’s mother.
: She owes Yuki some sort of debt? How? Yuki’s broke and your family practically owns this entire city.
: That’s a good question. She seems a bit reluctant to open up about their past. So much so that I might even think the two of them were partners if they weren’t so...heterosexual.
: I think your mom just likes having things to play with. And people are very interactive toys.
: They are, yes. But there’s much more to it than that. And I actually think she’d be quite distraught if anything happened to either you or Yuki.
: Well, at least I know who to turn to if I suddenly get cancer.
: Are you really sure you don’t know her, Sensei?
: No, you dunce. I mean on a level much greater than the one that began when she enrolled me in your class.
: For example, is it possible that you knew her before me and just happened to forget about her? Some sort of fleeting connection or something?
: That seems unlikely. There’s a lot about my past that’s sort of...intentionally fuzzy. But I have no idea where your mom would come into play or how we’d even cross paths at all.
: Hm. But what if she knew someone that you did? Yuki is somewhat close to your age, isn’t she?
: She’s got almost a decade on me, I think.
: Perhaps a family member then? I just can’t see why she’d be so interested if-
: I’d prefer not speaking about my family, if that’s okay.
: Out of discomfort or a lack of trust?
: I trust you. It just brings back bad memories.
: I see. Then perhaps we should take a reprieve from this conversation altogether and get something to eat.
: Is sushi okay? There’s a spot not far from here that I highly recommend. And I should be able to get us in despite the lack of a reservation given how important and wealthy I am.
: Will they not question someone like me accompanying you? You know, given how important and wealthy you are.
: I’m sure they will. But there’s a certain level of wealth one can reach where that’s no longer an issue since questioning anything about me would be intimidating given the difference in power.
: So you’re just allowed to get away with stuff other people wouldn’t?
: Essentially, yes.
: Maybe I’m secretly wealthy too then? Because I do that every day.
: Hurry up and find out, if you can. It’ll be far easier pitching our relationship to my father if you come from nobility.
: Or you could just...not do that. Fathers and me don’t really mix on account of how much sex I have with their daughters.
: Yes, brag some more, why don’t you? I’m not jealous or hormonal at all.
: You have servants to address that problem, I think.
: You’d hate that and you know it.
: I think you would too, to be honest.
: Heh.
: Probably even more than you.
Touka treats me to a fancy and surprisingly lengthy omakase course at a sushi restaurant that, no surprise, recognizes her immediately upon entry.
They seem more confused by her manner of dress than the fact that she’s accompanied by an older man, though, so I manage to dodge whatever bullet you’d associate with that.
Touka, unperturbed and elegant as ever, treats this like it’s completely normal, though. And that only further emphasizes the gap between us.
Which gets me thinking — if I do wind up with her by some stretch of fortune or disfortune based on how you look at it, would I feel this way forever? Would the gap always be this clear?
Or is there a point where it might become comforting? Where I could genuinely believe I’m something I’m not.
I take this question and expand on it, wondering how to rewrite it into some scenario where I can see myself as anything but scum.
But the final course comes before I think up an ending. And I find myself, once again, taken somewhere I shouldn’t be with someone who should have never taken me there at all.
: I’m surprised they just let you up here. I think I’d be a little more careful when it comes to the safety of an heiress, personally.
: My virginity is direct proof of that. Now, if only you’d offer the same chivalrous protection when it comes to my mental health. Why is my body the only thing you keep “safe,” Sensei?
: You really like me now, huh? You’re coming on strong tonight.

: Yes, well, I’ve been giving you signals for so long just to have them ignored that I feel like the time has come for me to flash my lights in your eyes to the point where you must address them posthaste.
: Ahh, so you brought me up here for sex. You really want your first time to be on a roof while that creepy billboard lady looks down on us?
: No one ever looks down on me. It doesn’t matter how high up they are.
: I do, sometimes.
: Ahh, then maybe that’s why I find you so attractive? You’re different.
: I don’t really mind if it’s you, though. I think I can handle being looked down on so long as it gets you to look at me.
: Oh, I look at you alright. You make it...quite difficult not to.
: Practice daily and it might become easier. Or not. Either way, I win.
: Sensei...I feel as if I need to address the situation with my sister. And I don’t know when the next chance I’ll get to do that is, so-
: You don’t need to, Touka. I know it makes you uncomfortable.
: Yes, it does. But it makes you uncomfortable as well. So I think we can both be a little uncomfortable for a moment if it helps...somehow lead to something good.
: Right. And how does this lead to anything good, exactly?
: Well, you know the situation, don’t you? Regarding Tsukasa and...her future both inside and...outside of the Tsukioka family.
: Tsukasa and I are not particularly close.
: We never have been as we were never really given the chance to be.
: Our schedules were just far too different and, with me being groomed into the future matriarch of my family, putting the two of us together for the sake of socialization just seemed like a waste.
: But she is still my sister. And the thought of her being used as a tool like this infuriates me. Even if she often infuriates me as well.
: If only your mother felt the same.
: I think she does.
: I don’t think she wants to do this, but I think she has to for some reason.
: Which is utterly absurd to me since there’s no family I can think of that can give us anything we don’t already have.
: And this...nonsense. What with you tutoring her on the topic of sexual education...that’s the most absurd thing of all.
: Like, I understand you being her tutor for other subjects. Tsukasa has taken a liking to you and doesn’t see our father often, so you’ve basically taken over as the man in her life.
: Well, maybe your father should start actually being a father. No offense.
: There should be offense. And the fact that he’d allow this to happen disgusts me. Perhaps even more than the fact that my mother would seemingly endorse it.

: That said...I think choosing you is an act of self-sabotage, in a sense. Like she’s screaming at you to ruin this arrangement, but the single sliver of pride you still possess is telling you not to.
: That’s exactly right. The last part, at least. I have barely anything left and it’s like she’s trying to set it on fire and leave me with literally nothing.
: I hope you know she doesn’t want that for you, Sensei. She does care.
: Then she should act like it and respect my boundaries. Teasing a starved lion with raw meat is just fucked up.
: The fact that you’d describe yourself as a “starved lion” is quite dark, isn’t it? You want the raw meat.
: Of course I want the raw meat. I’m a fucking carnivore.
: A vampire starved of human blood who must now feast on animals to survive. Who knows that biting humans is wrong, but still feels the temptation to do so.
: Bingo.
: And I am an animal.
: More like some kind of hybrid. I shouldn’t be drinking your blood either, but I’m going to anyway.
: Mm...you poor thing, you.
: Don’t give me your pity, please. That’s not going to help.
: I know that. But I’m not going to shy away from expressing myself just because you don’t like said expression.
: This is tough for me too, you know. I have fallen for you and it seems that, right now, the only way to save my sister from her fate is for you to take her.
: There has to be another way. I don’t get it.
: Yes...neither do I. And I feel as if I won’t understand for a very long time...
: But my mother seems to believe that you are the answer for some reason. And everything I’ve learned about you pushes me to think she’s right. I just don’t know why.

: Perhaps you are special in some way? And that this...indebted manner of which she approaches your relationship transcends the way it appears to us and actually makes sense when you have all the pieces?
: What “pieces” could make this make sense, Touka?
: Do you know what I heard the other day, Sensei?
: Beats me. But if it’s about who your sister is getting peddled onto, I don’t want to know.
: It was something about Ami. Her mother, specifically. Does that pique your interest?
: Oh, it appears that it does.
: What could you have possibly heard about her and why? She has nothing to do with you.
: It was just a rumor. Quite a morbid one, at that. Something about her body being buried beneath my family’s sakura tree.
: What?...
: Have you heard anything about that?
: Uhh...no? What? Why? How? It’s not...there’s no way that’s...I mean, I visit her grave. She and my brother are both-
: It’s not true. My mother assured me of it. But there’s apparently a poem she left behind about being buried beneath one that led Nodoka of all people to my family’s manor.
: It seems she’s quite interested in this matter.
: Yeah, well...Nodoka’s interested in a lot of things she shouldn’t be. And if she’s curious about Ami’s mom, she’s learned a much easier way to find things out.
: What a peculiar thing to say. I’d love to ask you more about it if you were not so upset right now.
: I’m not upset. I know where to find her if I ever become interested in necrophilia.
: You loved her dearly, didn’t you? That’s where this mother thing comes from.
: Then...
: Is Ami your daughter? Or are you really just her uncle?
: She’s not mine.
: Do you know for sure?
: She’s not mine.
: What does any of this have to do with Tsukasa, Touka? Why are you bringing her up, of all people?
: I just wonder if she and my mother were acquainted. It would sure explain a lot of things, wouldn’t it?
: Like what?
: This apparent and alleged debt, for one. Perhaps the two of them had some sort of promise?
: A promise? What, like, “Hey, if I ever suddenly die, make sure you get the boy I’m having sex with to fuck your daughters?” Sounds perfectly logical.
: There’s no need to get sarcastic with me. I know how ridiculous this all sounds.
: I’m just saying...it would be a very convenient way to tie all of this together and have it make some amount of sense.
: I still don’t think it makes any sense at all. And that having me do anything sexual with Tsukasa, whether it be teaching or defiling her, will do way more harm than good.
: It’s hard to ever know for sure. There are many things out there even scarier than me. Things we can’t and won’t understand. Things bigger than us. That can’t be conquered with logic alone.
: You don’t have to tell me twice...I experience just that all the fucking time.
: You could always lie, you know.
: What?...
: Take a page out of my mother’s book. If the truth isn’t convenient enough, just make up your own version of it.
: Perhaps it’s more important for people to believe that you and Tsukasa have crossed some sort of line than it is for you to actually cross it?
: Why involve me at all then? Why can’t she just lie on her own?
: Perhaps she needs to believe it too? I don’t know. These are all just ideas.
: But what I said sounds far better than what she proposed, yes? Even if you are some sort of vampire.
: I mean...yeah. If it’s that easy, I’ll gladly do it. I don’t want Tsukasa getting married off, either. I just know it won’t be that easy.
: Just out of curiosity, have you ever seen or read “Twilight,” Sensei?
: Is that another horror movie, or something?
: In a sense, yes. Though, mostly just because it’s terrible. But there’s something that happens in one of the books that seems somewhat relevant here. And it raises an interesting question.
: If someone you cared for was dying, and the only way to save them was by sinking your fangs into their flesh, could you do it?
: It would only have to be once. And no one would think any less of you. Why, you’d be a hero.
: It would just also change the person you bit for the rest of their life.
: Just some food for thought. I know you’ll find a way to solve this problem at the end of the day. And, once you do, you can keep the methodology employed a secret from me.
: Why me? Why do I have to solve this problem? I’m not even a part of your family.
: Not in name or blood, no. But you are a part of us, Sensei. Akira.
: Whether you like it not, we’ve already abducted you. We’re just kind enough to let you roam around on your own.
: I hate rich people. You guys find it way too easy to turn the rest of us into puppets.
: Hah! Oh, please. Your strings are far too tangled for any of us to manipulate them at all. All we can do is just poke you and make you swing or sway a little.
: Well, could you quit it? Life was easier before I had to figure out whether or not to have sex with a little girl.
: And when was that, I wonder? When did all of this begin?
: I have no reason to tell you that...
: No, I suppose you don’t. But you will. In time.
: After all, what’s the point of having a mother if you can’t confide in her?
: Touka-
: I apologize. I’ve rambled a bit too much when we should be cherishing a view like this, yes? It’ll only gray with time.
: Which means that, one day, we likely won’t see color at all. And that these moments of wistful splendor will pass like a mild sunshower.
: Which isn’t much of a problem for me, of course. I always carry an umbrella just in case.
: It’d be nice to have someone to hold it for me, though. Someone who might glisten under the light of the sun.
: Vampires die in the sun, Touka.
: Heh...
: Maybe you and I should watch Twilight next.
: Hah...
: You know, it’s funny.
: I feel as if there’s something I want to say here. And that, in another life, I probably could. Probably would.
: But it seems wrong in this one. And that if I say anything at all that tears us away from here and now, I might wind up regretting it for the rest of my life.
: So you just won’t say anything, then?
: Will you? Did I jump the gun and break the silence before you could confess your love to me?
: Yeah. Which is really unfortunate, because I’ve questioned everything over the last thirty seconds and just don’t really think I have it in me to actually do that now.
: Alas, my incessant need to draw your attention has spelled my downfall once more.
: Will this life ever get better for me?
: Better than being the richest girl in Kumon-mi? Who can get a seat at any restaurant and wander onto any roof except the one that matters?
: Yes, I- wait a moment. Which roof is the one that matters? What does that even mean?
: Something that would make your life definitively worse if you knew. So perhaps I should go back to keeping my mouth shut and just let you ramble a little longer.
: Heh...I’m not sure if that’s a good idea.
: For I feel quite compelled to say something very stupid right now.
We stay up there for another hour or two, just looking out at the lights and wondering if and when they’ll turn off.
The streets are even emptier now than they were before, and it’s only getting worse.
But even with how “bad” it gets, there’s one thing that doesn’t change.
Her confident silence. How she’s invisible until she speaks, even with how massive her presence is as both a girl and a woman.
And I hate that I see her that way.
But I love how I see her that way.
Yet I’ll never understand this peculiar way she sees me.
